summary: Full-extraction pass over 12 St Kitts and Nevis documents: four CBI regulations (S.R.O. 26 of 2023, 20 and 43 of 2024, 1 of 2026), the 2023 Exclusion Order, two SKNIS pages, two FAOSTAT sugar extracts, two IMF reports and an OECS report on sugar workers. Adds the fee schedules, dependant prices, agent fees and transition fees the first pass left out, four rule-change events, a 60-70% revenue-share claim, and FAOSTAT raw-sugar exports for 2008-2022.

events.title: New CBI regulations enacted; underselling criminalised
events.description: The Prime Minister says new CBI regulations were enacted by 23 December 2022, introducing a Board of Governors to oversee the CIU and a Technical Committee to review files, and criminalising underselling. The government had received a first report of its investigation into the programme in October 2022 and announced reforms in Dubai on 1 December 2022.
events.quote: By December 23, 2022, we enacted new CBI regulations into law.

events.title: Agents licensed yearly; marketing agents paid from each SISC contribution
events.description: S.R.O. 26 of 2023 requires Authorised Agents to apply each year (US$5,000) and International Marketing Agents to be designated (US$20,000 a year, up from US$10,000). For each Sustainable Island State Contribution application the Unit pays US$5,000 to the Authorised Agent and US$20,000 to the International Marketing Agent. Agent commissions and fees are excluded from minimum investments, circumventing a minimum is punishable by a fine of up to EC$10,000, and advertising the programme or showing its passport is restricted. Real estate bought under the programme cannot be resold for seven years.
events.quote: the Unit shall, on approval in writing from the Technical Committee and upon receipt of an invoice, pay to the following persons associated with the CBI application

events.title: CBI regulations reissued: US$50,000 agent payment, wider checks, advertising bans
events.description: S.R.O. 20 of 2024 replaces the 2023 regulations. For each SISC application the Unit now pays US$50,000 to the Authorised Agent. Due diligence must include checks by the national Financial Intelligence Unit, the Continuing International Due Diligence Unit, CARICOM IMPACS's Joint Regional Communications Centre and at least one international firm; insufficient proof of source of funds bars approval. Decisions in principle are due within 120 to 180 days (was 120). Schedule 2 bans advertising that names visa-free destinations or their number, speaks of "second" or "golden" passports, offers discounts or refers to the number or origin of successful applicants. Payments for real estate and public benefit units go through the Unit or an attorney and into escrow only after citizenship is granted.
events.quote: pay US$50,000 to the Authorised Agent associated with the CBI application

events.title: Parents aged 55 or over qualify as dependants; bankruptcy bar limited to ten years
events.description: S.R.O. 43 of 2024 lowers the age at which a parent of the main applicant or spouse counts as a dependant from 65 to 55, limits the bankruptcy bar to bankruptcies within ten years of the application, recomposes the Technical Committee (including a civil servant recommended by the Continuing International Due Diligence Unit and the CIU chief executive), and adds a US$7,500 fee for adding a child under three born after citizenship was granted.
events.quote: replacing the expression “sixty-five” with the expression “fifty-five” in paragraph (d).

No programme numbers (prices, fees, counts or money). The address itself (linked CBI.pdf) is a separate stored source (kna-ciu-address-2022-12).
ledger.notes: Needs a decision: the existing event from this source ('New CBI regime: Board of Governors, Technical Committee; SGF limited-time offer') says the SGF contribution was cut to US$125,000 for 1 Jan-30 Jun 2023, but this article does not mention the SGF or any price; that part comes from the CIU address (kna-ciu-address-2022-12). ledger.contains: Prime Minister's 'State of the CBI' speech of 17 Oct 2024: CBI revenue to the Federal Government 2019-2023 and Jan-Sep 2024 (already recorded); CBI said to have contributed 60-70 percent of Federal revenue when the government took office (Aug 2022); reform timeline (first investigation report Oct 2022, Dubai announcement 1 Dec 2022, new regulations by 23 Dec 2022, US-Caribbean roundtable Feb 2023, minimum raised to US$250,000 by July 2023, regional MoA March 2024); 'Prison Project' claim; list of planned projects (one, a new Basseterre High School, said to be CBI-funded, no amount). Rest is political programme, out of scope.

S.R.O. 1 of 2026 (16 Jan 2026): new definition of dependant (unmarried children 18-29 substantially supported) and a replacement regulation 26 setting post approval-in-principle application fees: US$25,000 per main applicant or family of up to four, US$25,000 per additional dependant under 18, US$50,000 per additional dependant 18+, US$30,000 to add a spouse/dependant after approval-in-principle, US$7,500 per child under 3 born after citizenship; the Public Benefit fee is deducted from the US$250,000. All fee lines now recorded; event already recorded.

S.R.O. 20 of 2024 (8 Jul 2024), the full CBI regulations replacing S.R.O. 26 of 2023: Technical Committee, eligibility bars, interviews, due diligence (FIU, CIDDU, JRCC, an international firm), four options with minimums (real estate US$400,000; SISC US$250,000 for up to four persons plus US$25,000/US$50,000 per extra dependant; private real estate US$400,000 condo/share, US$800,000 single-family; public benefit US$250,000), due diligence fees (US$10,000 / US$7,500), processing fee US$250 per applicant, post-approval application fees, US$50,000 paid by the Unit to the agent per SISC application, agent and marketing-agent annual fees (US$5,000 / US$20,000), transition fees for applications under the 2011 options, EC$10,000 fines, advertising prohibitions (Schedule 2). All amounts recorded as rules; one rule-change event added.

S.R.O. 26 of 2023 (27 Jul 2023), CBI regulations: Board of Governors, Technical Committee, eligibility, interviews, due diligence, four options with minimums (real estate US$400,000; SISC US$250,000 / US$300,000 / US$350,000 plus US$50,000 or US$75,000 per extra dependant; private homes US$400,000 condo, US$800,000 single-family; public benefit US$250,000), due diligence fees, US$250 processing fee, post-approval application fees (not on SISC), US$5,000 and US$20,000 paid by the Unit to agents per SISC application, agent annual fees (US$5,000; marketing agents US$20,000, previously US$10,000), transition fees and investment amounts for applications under the 2011 options (US$200,000 / US$175,000), EC$10,000 fines, seven-year resale bar. All amounts recorded; one rule-change event added.

S.R.O. 27 of 2023 Exclusion Order (27 Jul 2023): citizens and ordinary residents of Russia, Belarus, North Korea, Afghanistan, Iraq and Iran excluded from CBI applications. No numbers; event already recorded.

S.R.O. 43 of 2024 (25 Oct 2024) amending the 2024 regulations: parent dependants from age 55 (was 65); Technical Committee membership; bankruptcy bar limited to 10 years; real estate minimum US$325,000 (was US$400,000); private real estate US$325,000 condo/share and US$600,000 single-family (were US$400,000 / US$800,000); SISC wording; appraiser rule; new US$7,500 fee for a child under 3 born after citizenship. Fee and rule-change event added; price rows already recorded.

FAOSTAT production extract for St Kitts and Nevis: sugar cane production 1961-2006 and raw sugar production 1961-2005 (all already recorded); also sugar cane area harvested and yield, and the 'Sugar Crops Primary' aggregate (identical to sugar cane). Area and yield are not recorded: no indicator in this dataset, and they are agricultural context rather than programme numbers.

FAOSTAT trade extract for St Kitts and Nevis sugar items 1961-2024. Raw sugar export value and quantity 1961-2007 were already recorded; this pass adds 2008-2017 and 2022 (residual trade after the 2005 closure; no values printed for 2018-2021 or 2023-2024). Not recorded (no indicator, not export of raw sugar): imports of all sugar items, and exports of refined sugar, sugar confectionery, 'sugar and syrups n.e.c.', 'Sugar and Honey' and 'Sugar Crops Primary' aggregates, and other sugar crops.

IMF 2006 Article IV staff report on St Kitts and Nevis (CR 07/141): sugar closure context (losses 3-4% of GDP, 9,300 acres, about 1,400 workers or 6% of labour force, SSMC debt 29% of GDP), Box 1 on closure costs (severance EC$27.4 million for 1,406 workers, EC$22.5 million paid in 2005; 30-year bond; 4,700 acres collateral; sugar exports 2.5% of GDP 2000-04; 317 former workers unemployed in mid-2006), EU aid EUR 1.3 billion, Table 4 SSMC debt 2001-05, Table 5 sugar exports 2001-05. No CBI content (the 2006 report does not mention the programme). Adds the EC$22.5 million paid in 2005; all other sugar numbers that fit an indicator were already recorded. Not recorded (no indicator, not programme numbers): severance as a share of GDP (2% 2005, 0.5% 2006, 2.3% of 2005 GDP), land acreages, interest cost of the SSMC debt (1.5% of GDP), 317 unemployed former workers, macro tables.
